description: PROC GLMSELECT SELECTION=LASSO -> scikit-learn LassoLarsIC/LassoLarsCV, matching the CHOOSE=/STOP= criterion and standardization.

glmselect_lasso.title: SELECTION=LASSO -> LassoLarsIC / LassoLarsCV; match CHOOSE=SBC->bic, AIC->aic; standardize by default.
rule: `PROC GLMSELECT` fits a linear model with automated variable selection; `SELECTION=LASSO` uses the LASSO path.
Python equivalent: `sklearn.linear_model.LassoLarsIC` or `LassoCV`; the LARS path (`LassoLarsCV`) matches SAS most closely.

Match the SAS `CHOOSE=`/`STOP=` criterion: `CHOOSE=SBC` -> `LassoLarsIC(criterion="bic")`, `CHOOSE=AIC` -> `LassoLarsIC(criterion="aic")`, `CVMETHOD=...` -> `LassoLarsCV`/`LassoCV` with matching folds.
GLMSELECT **standardizes predictors by default** (`NOSTANDARDIZE` turns it off). Use `StandardScaler` unless NOSTANDARDIZE is present.
CLASS variables -> one-hot encode (`pd.get_dummies`) with SAS reference-level coding.
`OUTEST=` captures the selected coefficients; reproduce that table (names + estimates) for QC.
pitfalls: Exact coefficient parity is unlikely; the selected-variable set and QC tolerances matter more than bit-identical betas.
Skipping standardization changes which variables enter the LASSO path.

code: Xs = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)              # GLMSELECT standardizes by default
